span.term: Descent fails because every compact Hausdorff space is covered by a profinite set, and sheaves on profinite sets are already Postnikov complete while sheaves on a general compact Hausdorff space are not, so the target of the limit is forced to satisfy a completeness the source lacks.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Three competing sheaf theories agree on all truncated objects, so which one a result used is invisible until unbounded objects are involved.
span.note: what this limits: a result stated for sheaves on a space: sheaves, hypersheaves and Postnikov complete sheaves all have the same truncated objects, and the differences between the three theories appear only on unbounded objects - so two such results can be compared safely in the truncated case and not otherwise

span.label: Two incompatible set-theoretic foundations are in use in this literature; the difference is declared inessential and then not mentioned again.
span.note: what this limits: a comparison between results in this paper and results of Clausen and Scholze: the two use different set-theoretic foundations, one with universes and one avoiding them, which the author states is a minor difference not affecting any argument in an essential way
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The agreement between three cohomology theories is claimed for spaces satisfying a stated structural condition, not in general.
span.note: what this limits: the claim that condensed and sheaf cohomology agree: the three-way agreement is asserted for a topological space admitting a locally finite CW structure, so it is a conditional identification rather than a general one

span.label: For a compactly assembled coefficient ∞-category, the assignment of the ∞-category of Postnikov complete sheaves to a locally compact Hausdorff space satisfies descent along proper surjections.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The same result gives proper descent for left complete derived ∞-categories and shows that Postnikov complete sheaves form a sheaf on compact Hausdorff spaces for the topology of finite jointly surjective families.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Neither ordinary sheaves nor hypersheaves define a sheaf of ∞-topoi on the site of compact Hausdorff spaces, so the descent statement genuinely fails without Postnikov completion.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Postnikov complete sheaves on a locally compact Hausdorff space embed fully faithfully into condensed objects over that space.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Consequently the sheaf cohomology and the condensed cohomology of a locally compact Hausdorff space coincide.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: For a space carrying a locally finite CW structure, condensed, singular and sheaf cohomology all coincide.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Sheaves on a profinite set are Postnikov complete, whereas sheaves on the Hilbert cube are not, so Postnikov completeness is not automatic for compact Hausdorff spaces.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The protruncated shape functor on compact Hausdorff spaces fails to preserve pullbacks, even though it preserves finite coproducts, cofiltered limits and Čech-nerve realizations.
